I have a complete picture of the date rolling logic. Here are my findings.

## Core adjustment logic (production)

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/ResolveRegistrationDate.java`**

This is the class that adjusts a registration date to a business day. It resolves the effective date (request-supplied `registrationDate`, else `LocalDate.now()`) and rolls weekends forward, then publishes the adjusted `LocalDate` for downstream steps.

The actual roll happens in the `static LocalDate toBusinessDay(LocalDate date)` method (lines 29-38):
- Saturday -> `+2 days` (to Monday)
- Sunday -> `+1 day` (to Monday)
- Any weekday -> unchanged

Note it uses fixed offsets rather than a loop, and only handles weekends.

## Related production code

- **`.../rest/function/owner/EnsureRegistrationDateNotFuture.java`** — rejects a supplied future `registrationDate` with 400 (before resolution). Validates only when present.
- **`.../rest/function/owner/BuildOwner.java`** (line 16-18) — stamps the resolved/rolled `registrationDate` onto the `Owner`.
- **`.../rest/function/owner/CountDailyRegistrations.java`** — counts owners sharing the resolved registration date.
- **`.../rest/function/owner/EnsureDailyRegistrationLimit.java`** — enforces per-business-day cap against the resolved date.
- **`.../rest/function/owner/AssignMembershipNumber.java`** and **`AssignMembership.java`** — derive membership values from the registration date.
- **`.../rest/escalation/FutureRegistrationDateException.java`** and **`FutureRegistrationDateExceptionHandler.java`** — the 400 escalation for future dates.
- **`.../model/Owner.java`** (lines 66, 167-172) — the `registrationDate` field/getter/setter.

## Tests

There is **no dedicated unit test** for `ResolveRegistrationDate` / `toBusinessDay`. The only coverage is a black-box acceptance test:

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java`** — test `coreDefaultDateIsBusinessDay()` (lines 14-19) creates an owner with the default date and asserts the returned `registrationDate` is not a Saturday or Sunday. It asserts only the weekend invariant.

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java`** — the shared test base:
- `HOLIDAYS` constant (lines 239-242): a fixed set of 2026 public holidays.
- `toBusinessDay(LocalDate d)` helper (lines 267-274): a **loop** that rolls forward over `SATURDAY`, `SUNDAY`, **and `HOLIDAYS`**.

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AuditLogCapture.java`** — test support (matched on "roll"/"adjust" generically; not date-rolling specific).

## Discrepancy worth flagging

There is a likely bug / spec mismatch. The test documentation and the test helper describe holiday handling:
- `AcceptanceTest.java` header comment (lines 9-11): "the default registration date rolls past public holidays as well as weekends."
- `AcceptanceBase.toBusinessDay` skips `HOLIDAYS` in addition to weekends.

But the production `ResolveRegistrationDate.toBusinessDay` (lines 29-38) **only handles weekends and does not skip holidays**. Additionally, because it uses fixed `+2`/`+1` offsets instead of a loop, it cannot roll further even if a holiday landed on the target Monday. The acceptance test only asserts the weaker "not Sat/Sun" invariant, so it would not catch the missing holiday logic.

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/owners.POST.yml`, `.../openapi.yml`, and the `schema.sql` files under `.../resources/db/{h2,hsqldb,mysql,postgres}/` also reference `registration_date`/`registrationDate` but contain no rolling logic.
